deviceOnlyBody.message: Your accounts are protected only by a key stored next to them. That stops casual reading but not someone, or malware, with access to this browser profile. With a master password, a copy of the profile is as safe as the password you choose.

newCodeBody.message: Replaces the current key, which stops working.

rotateBody.message: Use this if you think an old copy of your data or key may have leaked. Everything is re-encrypted with a new key and you get a new recovery key.

autoLockNote.message: Applies when a master password is set. Updating or reloading the extension always locks it.

residueWarning.message: Accounts you added before turning this on may still be recoverable from leftover data on disk until the browser compacts its storage. If this browser profile was ever copied or shared, re-issue those accounts' 2FA keys at each service.

secLead.message: How your accounts are protected on this computer, and what happens when you lock.

smLead.message: Two ready-made sets of the settings below, the same as the question when Sixkey was set up. Change any one of them and the mode shows as Custom.

smCustomBody.message: Your own choice of the settings below. Pick a mode above to go back to it.

smClipNote.message: In a shared or automated profile, also clear the clipboard after each copy:

smLockedNow.message: Sixkey is locked now. Unlock it at the top of this page to go on.

secNoticeBad.message: The security record can't be read.

secLogLead.message: Wrong passwords, exports and key changes in this browser profile, with the time only. An alert, not evidence: anyone with a copy of the profile can change it.

secLogCount.message: Wrong attempts not yet shown after an unlock: $1

secLogDamaged.message: It is damaged. The next entry starts a new one.

secLogNewer.message: A newer version of Sixkey wrote it. This version does not add to it.

secLogClearLead.message: Needs your PIN, or your master password when there is no PIN. A wrong one is refused and recorded. One dated line stays.

secKPasswordReset.message: Master password reset with the recovery key

secInvTitle.message: What Sixkey keeps in this browser profile

secInvKeysPw.message: Your accounts, encrypted, and the key that opens them, locked by your master password and by your recovery key.

secInvKeysDevice.message: Your accounts, encrypted, and the key that opens them, kept beside them unlocked: a copy of this profile opens them.

secInvSnaps.message: $1 older encrypted copies (the last 10 saves, one a day for 7 days).

secInvMirror.message: A second encrypted copy, and up to 7 daily ones, in this profile's IndexedDB.

secInvNoMirror.message: No copy found in this profile's IndexedDB.

secInvSettings.message: Settings: locking, display, language, theme, any install warning, an ID that orders edits, upkeep markers (no keys), and the last backup ($1).

secInvLogs.message: This record, notes of automatic restores, and a log of minor problems. None holds keys, codes or account names.

secInvSession.message: While unlocked: the opened key, in the browser's memory-only session storage (not when locking every time).

secKPrfEnrolled.message: Unlock with Touch ID or Windows Hello added

secKPrfRemoved.message: Unlock with Touch ID or Windows Hello removed

secKPrfFailed.message: Unlocking with Touch ID or Windows Hello failed

pinLead.message: A PIN of 4 to 8 digits opens Sixkey again after it locks, also after the browser restarts. Don't reuse your phone or bank PIN.

pinHonest.message: A PIN stops people at your computer: after 5 wrong tries only the master password opens Sixkey. It does not stop programs on this computer, or anyone who opens the browser's developer tools.

pinRoot.message: The master password always works. While the PIN opens Sixkey, exports, deleting for good and changing the PIN ask for the PIN again; key changes ask for the master password.

pinClose.message: To lock whenever the popup closes, choose “$1” under Automatic lock. The PIN opens it again.

pinWaiting.message: On ($1 digits). It works again after you next type the master password.

pinShared.message: Not available: this profile is declared shared or controlled by scripts (Security mode), and they could read a PIN.

quickEnded.message: Ended. Sixkey is locked, and the master password opens it.
